name: Emnes Backup Migrate Reset
author: akdevs

sections.description:
Emnes Backup Migrate Reset is a modern, developer-friendly WordPress plugin that provides complete site backup, migration, restoration, and database reset capabilities — all from a clean admin interface or via REST API and WP-CLI.

Built with PHP 8.1 strict types, a service container architecture, and WordPress coding standards, it’s designed for reliability, security, and extensibility.

Backup

  • Full Site Backup — Back up your database, plugins, themes, uploads, and WordPress core files with one click.
  • Component Selection — Choose exactly which parts of your site to include in each backup.
  • Split Archives — Large directories are automatically split into 200 MB ZIP parts; backups run in a background process so web-server timeouts cannot interrupt them.
  • Backup Verification — Verify any backup’s integrity with checksum validation.
  • Retention Policies — Automatically clean up old backups by count or age.

Restore

  • Selective Restore — Choose which components to restore from any backup.
  • Search & Replace — Automatic URL replacement during migration between domains.
  • Safe Database Restore — A safety snapshot of the current database is taken first; a failed import is rolled back automatically. Foreign key checks are handled for you.

Database Reset

  • Full Reset — Reset your WordPress database to a fresh installation state.
  • Reactivation Options — Optionally reactivate your current theme and plugins after reset.
  • Safety Confirmation — You must type RESET and the server verifies it; on multisite only the current sub-site is reset.

Migration

  • Import/Export — Export backups as downloadable ZIPs and import on another site.
  • Domain Migration — Automatic URL search-and-replace handles domain changes.
  • Security — Imported archives are validated against size limits to prevent abuse.

Developer Tools

  • REST API — Full REST API (ebmr/v1) for programmatic access.
  • WP-CLI — Create, list, verify, and delete backups from the command line.
  • Audit Log — Every operation is logged with user, timestamp, and details.
  • Progress Tracking — Real-time progress updates with adaptive polling.
  • Hooks & Filters — Extensible with actions and filters for every operation.

Pro Add-on

Unlock additional capabilities with the Emnes Backup Migrate Reset Pro add-on:

  • Scheduled Backups — Automated hourly, daily, or weekly backups via WordPress cron.
  • Cloud Storage — Store backups on Amazon S3, Google Drive, Dropbox, or SFTP servers.
  • Email Notifications — Get notified on backup success or failure.
  • Encrypted Credentials — All cloud storage secrets are encrypted at rest.

External Services

Freemius SDK

This plugin uses the Freemius SDK for license management, add-on discovery, and optional usage tracking. Freemius may collect non-sensitive diagnostic data (such as PHP version, WordPress version, plugin version, and site URL) to help improve compatibility and support. This data is only transmitted if the user explicitly opts in during the plugin activation process.

What data is sent: Non-sensitive diagnostic data (PHP version, WordPress version, plugin version, site URL) when the user opts in. No personal content or database data is ever transmitted.

When: During plugin activation (opt-in prompt) and periodically for license validation and update checks.

Service provider: Freemius, Inc.
– Terms of Service: https://freemius.com/terms/
– Privacy Policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/
sections.installation:
From WordPress Admin

  1. Download the plugin ZIP file.
  2. Go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin in your WordPress admin.
  3. Upload the ZIP file and click Install Now.
  4. Activate the plugin.
  5. Navigate to Emnes Backup Migrate Reset in the admin sidebar.

Manual Installation

  1. Upload the emnes-backup-migrate-reset folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to the Emnes Backup Migrate Reset menu item in your admin panel.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.0 or higher
  • PHP 8.1 or higher
  • zip PHP extension (for file backups)
sections.faq:
What does this plugin back up?

Your database, plugins, themes, uploads directory, and WordPress core files. Each component can be selected individually.

Where are backups stored?

Backups are stored on your server in a private directory. When the directory above your web root is writable the plugin uses it; otherwise it creates a directory with a random, non-guessable name inside wp-content/uploads/emnes-backup-migrate-reset/, protected by .htaccess (Apache) and index.php. On Nginx the Server Health page shows a ready-to-paste location rule, and you can move the store anywhere with define('EBMR_BACKUP_BASE_DIR', '/path/outside/web/root'); in wp-config.php. Archives are downloaded only through authenticated plugin endpoints. With the Pro add-on, copies are also uploaded to Amazon S3, Google Drive, Dropbox or an SFTP server.

Can I migrate my site to a new domain?

Yes. Export your backup from the source site, import it on the destination site, and the plugin will automatically perform search-and-replace on URLs during restoration. No manual database editing required.

Is there a REST API?

Yes. The plugin provides a full REST API under the ebmr/v1 namespace covering backup, restore, reset, import/export, settings, and progress tracking. All endpoints require an administrator (a Super Admin on multisite) and a REST nonce.

Does it support WP-CLI?

Yes. Available commands include:
* wp ebmr backup create — Create a backup with optional component selection
* wp ebmr backup list — List all backups in table, JSON, or CSV format
* wp ebmr backup verify — Verify a backup’s integrity
* wp ebmr backup restore — Restore a backup (with safety snapshot and optional URL search-replace)
* wp ebmr backup delete — Delete a backup

Is this plugin multisite compatible?

Yes, with a deliberately strict model: on a multisite network only Super Admins can use the plugin, because restores write to directories and tables shared by the whole network. Each site is backed up from its own dashboard (the main site’s backup includes the network tables, never the sub-sites’ tables). Database reset is available for sub-sites only. Uninstall cleanup runs across all sites in the network.

What happens when I uninstall the plugin?

All plugin options, audit log entries and locks are removed. Your backup archives are kept on the server unless you enable “Delete backups when the plugin is uninstalled” in Settings > Retention first.

How does backup verification work?

Each backup component generates a checksum during creation. The verify endpoint recalculates checksums and compares them against stored values to detect corruption or tampering.

Is there a file size limit for imports?

Yes. Imported ZIP archives are validated against a 2 GB total size limit and 512 MB per-file limit to prevent ZIP bomb attacks, and only recognised backup files (database dump, component archives, manifest, checksums) are extracted. The limits are configurable via the ebmr_import_max_* filters.

Can I restore a backup made with an older plugin version?

Yes. Backups carry a format version instead of a plugin version; every backup made with an older or the same format restores after updating the plugin. Only backups created by a newer plugin release ask you to update first.

Which files are never included in a backup?

wp-config.php, .env files, .maintenance, .git/.svn/node_modules folders, cache directories and the backup store itself are excluded by default (filter: ebmr_default_excludes).

Is this a replacement for UpdraftPlus or Duplicator?

For most sites, no: those are mature backup suites. Choose this plugin when you reset or rebuild sites often, work from the command line, or need the REST API; its backups exist so that every reset and migration is reversible.

Can I reset a site from WP-CLI?

Yes. The wp ebmr command group covers backups, restores and resets; run wp help ebmr for the exact subcommands and options. A safety snapshot is taken before a reset so it can be undone.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • Uninstall cleanup now runs through the Freemius SDK’s after_uninstall hook (no root uninstall.php); no functional change.

1.1.0

  • Data integrity: the database dump now paginates by the full primary key (composite and text keys included) and takes a consistent snapshot for tables without a key, so no rows are lost; values containing % are written correctly.
  • Data integrity: URL search-replace iterates by primary key instead of a shifting OFFSET, so no row is skipped; http/https/protocol-relative, JSON-escaped and URL-encoded variants are replaced; JSON columns are handled.
  • Safety: a database-only safety snapshot is taken before every database restore and the restore rolls back to it automatically if the import fails; schema statements that fail abort the import instead of continuing.
  • Safety: the SQL importer tokenises statements (quotes, comments), restricts them to the tables of the current site and refuses dumps made with a different table prefix.
  • Fixed: preserved options (site URL, home, blog name, admin e-mail) are really written back after a restore.
  • Fixed: restore no longer refuses backups made with another plugin version; a format version is checked instead.
  • Fixed: WordPress core and “other content” backups no longer archive the backup store itself; the store is excluded by real path, and a restore can never write over it.
  • Security: on multisite every operation requires a Super Admin; DISALLOW_FILE_MODS blocks restores that would write code.
  • Security: backups live in a private directory (above the web root when possible, otherwise a random, non-guessable directory in uploads) with Apache 2.2/2.4 rules; Nginx users get a ready-to-paste rule on the Server Health page.
  • Security: wp-config.php, .env, caches and VCS folders are excluded from file backups by default; restore logs no longer contain row data; imports extract only recognised backup files; downloads require capability and nonce.
  • Security: database reset requires the typed confirmation to be verified server-side and, on multisite, is limited to sub-sites.
  • Security: REST settings are sanitised through the same rules as the settings form; the settings body is validated.
  • Reliability: backups run in a background process (with automatic fallback) so a web-server timeout cannot kill them; progress is stored in a file and survives a database restore.
  • Reliability: the operation lock really prevents concurrent backups, restores and resets; stale-run detection uses a heartbeat and no longer flags live runs.
  • Reliability: the admin UI no longer reports a failed or interrupted restore as a success; it verifies the result through the progress endpoint.
  • New: “Other content” component (mu-plugins, languages and other wp-content files), wp ebmr backup restore command, per-backup remote-storage status for add-ons.
  • Changed: uninstall keeps backup archives unless you opt in to deleting them.
  • Changed: Freemius SDK 2.13.1 is bundled directly; Composer only provides the autoloader.
  • Removed dead code (unused scheduler, SQL-mode manager, unused enum members) and fixed broken admin links.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Full site backup with database, plugins, themes, and uploads.
  • Selective restore with component chooser.
  • Database reset with theme/plugin reactivation options.
  • Import/export for site migration with URL search-and-replace.
  • REST API with 14 endpoints for all operations.
  • WP-CLI commands for backup, list, verify, and delete.
  • Backup verification with checksum integrity checks.
  • Retention policies by max count and max age.
  • Audit log for tracking all operations.
  • Real-time progress tracking with adaptive polling.
  • ZIP bomb protection for imported archives.
  • Multisite-aware uninstall cleanup.
  • Accessibility: ARIA roles, keyboard navigation, screen reader support.
  • Freemius SDK integration for licensing and add-on management.
